title: India's Tourism Ministry Signs MoU With Google to Supercharge Incredible India Campaign With AI
excerpt: The partnership will use artificial intelligence, data-driven insights, and digital storytelling to promote Indian destinations globally, part of a broader push that includes Netflix films, Air India's expanding route network, and Mastercard collaboration.
body:
• India's Ministry of Tourism signed an MoU with Google India on July 11, 2026 to strengthen digital promotion of tourism destinations through AI, data analytics, and digital storytelling under the Incredible India initiative
  • The partnership is non-commercial and non-binding, focused on knowledge sharing, capacity building, and evidence-based tourism promotion using Google's travel trend insights
  • Air India has signed MoUs with Thai Airways, Riyadh Air, and the Lufthansa Group in 2026, expanding international connectivity to support tourism growth
  • The Ministry has also partnered with Netflix to produce ten promotional videos showcasing Indian destinations, with two films launched at ITB Berlin in March 2026

Digital Push for Incredible India

India's Ministry of Tourism signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Google India on July 11, establishing a framework to promote Indian tourism destinations through artificial intelligence, digital technologies, and data-driven marketing under the Incredible India campaign.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=CoEfikNZWGE

Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, who presided over the signing in New Delhi, described the collaboration as a shift toward technology-led tourism development. "Digital technologies have the potential to create immersive experiences that showcase India's cultural and heritage sites to audiences worldwide," he said, according to the Press Information Bureau.

The MoU is non-commercial, non-binding, and non-exclusive, with no financial implications for either party. Under the partnership, Google will provide insights into global travel trends, traveler behavior, and digital engagement patterns to support evidence-based tourism promotion strategies. The collaboration includes training programs for Ministry officials on digital marketing tools, AI applications, and campaign optimization.

"By harnessing cutting-edge digital technologies, we can transform the way travellers discover, experience and engage with India's rich cultural and natural heritage."

— Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture

A Broader Promotion Blitz

The Google partnership is one piece of a multi-pronged strategy the Ministry has been executing throughout 2026 to position India as a premier global travel destination.

At ITB Berlin in March, Shekhawat launched two promotional tourism films developed under a collaboration between Netflix and the Ministry of Tourism. The films — one celebrating India's vibrant culture, festivals, and heritage, the other showcasing Indian cuisine — are the first in a planned series of ten promotional videos. Each film uses cinematic visuals inspired by Netflix's Indian original content to create emotional engagement with potential travelers.

The Ministry has also signed an MoU with Mastercard to strengthen India's tourism appeal through curated digital payment experiences and destination-linked offerings. Tourism Australia signed a separate three-year marketing agreement with Air India to drive Indian visitor arrivals to Australia.

Air India's Connectivity Expansion

While the Ministry builds the brand, Air India has been building the network. The Tata Group-owned carrier signed MoUs with Thai Airways on June 7 in Rio de Janeiro, with Riyadh Air on June 9, and with the Lufthansa Group earlier in 2026 — each aimed at expanding codeshare arrangements and boosting international connectivity.

The Thai Airways partnership alone extends Air India's effective route reach to more than 30 countries across Asia, Europe, North America, and the Middle East. The codeshare arrangements will allow passengers to book multi-destination itineraries on a single ticket, a critical enabler for tourism flows.

Campbell Wilson, Air India's CEO and Managing Director, has framed the airline's expansion as directly supporting India's tourism ambitions. "This MoU supports Air India's broader ambition to strengthen India's connectivity with the world, offering our customers more choice and greater value," Wilson said at the Thai Airways signing.

The Numbers Behind the Push

India received 260,000 foreign tourist arrivals from Germany alone in 2025, making it the 8th largest source market, according to Ministry data shared at ITB Berlin. The government's goal is to establish India as a "365 days global travel destination" — moving beyond seasonal heritage tourism to year-round offerings spanning wellness, adventure, ecotourism, and culinary experiences.

The digital promotion strategy is designed to reach travelers before they decide on a destination. Google's travel trend data, combined with AI-powered content optimization, would allow the Ministry to target potential visitors with personalized content based on their browsing and search behavior — a significant upgrade from traditional tourism marketing through print brochures and trade show appearances.

What It Means for Indian Tourism

The convergence of digital promotion, airline connectivity, and entertainment partnerships represents India's most coordinated tourism push in years. For the diaspora community, improved Air India connectivity and destination visibility could make return visits easier and encourage friends and family abroad to add India to their travel plans. The test will be whether the partnerships translate into measurable increases in foreign tourist arrivals and tourism revenue.
nri_angle: Improved Air India connectivity and destination visibility through digital platforms could make return visits easier for the Indian diaspora and encourage friends and family abroad to discover India.
